AI-driven automation, predictive analytics and remote care boost efficiency and outcomes, while North America leads adoption and investment.

Dublin, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- "Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare Market Size and Share - Growth Analysis Report and Forecast Trends (2026-2035)" has been added to ResearchAndMarkets.com's offering.

The global artificial intelligence in healthcare market was valued at USD 21.06 Billion in 2025 and is projected to reach USD 571.12 Billion by 2035, expanding at a CAGR of 39.10% from 2026-2035. Market growth is being driven by rising healthcare data volumes, demand for greater cost efficiency, workforce shortages, and the adoption of AI-enabled automation across clinical and administrative workflows.

Healthcare organizations are increasingly deploying artificial intelligence to strengthen clinical decision support, predictive analytics, EHR integration, diagnostic imaging, personalized treatment planning, telemedicine, and remote patient monitoring. These applications are helping hospitals, laboratories, payers, and life sciences companies improve decision-making, reduce errors, optimize operations, and enhance patient outcomes.

Investment in AI Infrastructure Supports Market Expansion

Growing investment in high-performance AI infrastructure is accelerating healthcare research, predictive modeling, clinical trials, and workflow automation. In March 2026, Roche expanded its AI infrastructure through the deployment of more than 2,100 Nvidia GPUs across the United States and Europe. The investment is intended to enhance data modeling and AI workflow automation for research and clinical trials, supporting faster innovation and greater operational efficiency.

Demand for advanced computing capacity is also increasing as healthcare institutions adopt AI for medical imaging, genomics, drug discovery, and population health management. These investments are expected to strengthen AI integration across hospitals, diagnostic laboratories, pharmaceutical companies, and research centers throughout the forecast period.

AI-driven patient care is emerging as a significant market trend as providers expand telehealth, virtual assistance, patient engagement, and remote monitoring services. In March 2026, Doctronic raised USD 40 million to pilot AI tools for prescription refills and telehealth visits. AI-powered chatbots are also being adopted to support mental health and rehabilitation services.

These developments are expected to improve access to care, streamline routine interactions, and reduce administrative pressure on healthcare professionals. Continued adoption of digital health platforms will further increase demand for symptom management, medication reminders, post-treatment surveillance, and personalized care solutions.

The report analyzes integrated solutions, AI technologies, services, and niche/point solutions. Key functions include diagnosis and early detection, risk assessment and patient stratification, patient engagement and remote monitoring, pharmacy management, data management and analytics, administrative automation, cybersecurity, and treatment planning and personalization.

Applications are divided into clinical and non-clinical categories, while deployment modes include On Premise and Cloud Based solutions. Major technologies covered include Machine Learning, Deep Learning, Natural Language Processing, Context-aware Computing, Computer Vision, OCR (Optical Character Recognition), Auto Coding, Text Analytics, and Speech Analytics.

End users include healthcare providers, hospitals and clinics, Ambulatory Surgical Centers (ASCs), diagnostic and imaging centers, healthcare payers, pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies, medical device companies, and patients. The regional analysis covers North America, Europe, Asia Pacific, Latin America, and the Middle East and Africa.

North America maintained the largest market share, accounting for more than 54% of historical revenue. The region benefits from advanced healthcare infrastructure, early adoption of AI solutions, supportive government initiatives, substantial R&D investment, and the strong presence of technology, pharmaceutical, and medical device companies.

Pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies are expected to remain a major end-use segment as AI adoption expands across drug discovery, clinical trial design, predictive analytics, personalized medicine, and R&D workflow optimization. AI platforms can help companies improve research productivity, identify viable drug candidates, and accelerate development timelines.

Leading companies are strengthening their market positions through product development, funding, investment, partnerships, and other strategic initiatives. Koninklijke Philips N.V. applies AI to diagnostic imaging, predictive analytics, clinical decision-making, intensive care, and telehealth. Microsoft Corporation supports clinical documentation, EHR data extraction, virtual assistants, population health management, and predictive analytics through its cloud and AI capabilities.

NVIDIA Corporation provides GPU computing and AI platforms for image processing, predictive modeling, genomics, drug discovery, and telehealth. Siemens Healthineers AG integrates AI into diagnostic, laboratory, imaging, monitoring, and therapy workflows. Other key participants include GE Healthcare, Epic Systems Corporation, Oracle, Veradigm LLC, Medtronic plc, and Google.

The report also evaluates market drivers, opportunities, restraints, unmet needs, patent activity, funding trends, investment patterns, and the influence of partnerships, collaborations, mergers, and acquisitions on the competitive landscape.
